Use case: style-transfer. Edit targets: image 1 existing Ember fox animation sheet, image 2 existing swimming strip. Preserve this fox's identity, orange fur, cream muzzle/chest/tail tip, dark olive feet, bushy tail, proportions and expressive poses. Produce ONE unified 1024x1024 pixel-art atlas, exactly FOUR columns and FOUR rows of equal 256x256 cells. Read left to right. Row1 four alternating walking poses from image1. Row2 idle, crouched windup, leaping open-mouth bite, recovery. Row3 hurt recoil, death collapse1, collapse2, lying dead. Row4 the three swimming poses from image2 (extended reach, downward pull, tucked recovery); fourth cell EMPTY background. No text or borders. All face RIGHT, remain separate with empty margins, match scale across all fifteen poses, grounded feet share baseline.
CRITICAL raster specification: draw as if each tile is a native 32x32 pixel canvas enlarged EXACTLY 8x with nearest-neighbor. ONE SHARED GLOBAL GRID: every artistic pixel is an 8x8 uniformly flat square, edges only at multiples of 8. Every eye, nose, fur boundary, ear interior, outline and highlight must obey that same grid. Fox occupies about 20-24 logical pixels across including tail. Meaningful chunky anatomical clusters. Each material has at most shadow/base/highlight, about 9 opaque colors total. Flat earthy palette, dark brown/olive outlines. No sub-pixel texturing whatsoever. No finer squares inside the large squares, no fine fur, no gradients, no lighting noise, no blur, no antialiasing, no thin lines, no painterly grain. Redraw/simplify the art, do not just blur or enlarge the existing detail. Plain perfectly uniform #203640 background. Preserve leg differences, face readability and animation silhouette changes.
